title: Enhanced fluorescent imaging of proteins in live yeast cells using fluorescently labeled scFv
protocol: Digest 1–2 μg of the desired 2E2-FP plasmid with 0.5 μL of the appropriate restriction enzyme according to manufacturer’s guidelines.
Load 100 ng of the digested plasmid and a sample of 1 kb DNA ladder onto a 1% agarose gel, stained with SYBR SAFE DNA Gel Stain.
Run the gel for 30 min at 120 V.
Visualize the gel under blue light or UV lamp.
Inoculate yeast cells for transformation from an agar plate or frozen glycerol stock into 5 mL prewarmed YPD medium in a 50 mL falcon tube.
Grow yeast culture at 30°C in a shaker incubator.
Measure O.D.600 of the yeast culture and dilute cells to O.D.600 of 0.1 in 12 mL prewarmed YPD medium.
Incubate diluted yeast cells for approximately 3 hours or until O.D.600 reaches 0.35-0.50.
Centrifuge yeast culture at 3000 × g for 5 min.
Discard supernatant and wash twice with 10–15 mL ddH2O.
Resuspend washed cell pellet with 100 μL ddH2O.
Prepare a transformation reaction in an Eppendorf tube according to the protocol table.
Mix by inverting the transformation tube.
Vortex the transformation tube briefly.
Spin down the transformation tube briefly to collect solution from tube walls.
Incubate the transformation reaction at 42°C in a shaker for 40–60 min.
Centrifuge cells at 12000 × g for 1 min.
Discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 1–2 mL prewarmed YPD medium.
Transfer resuspended cells to a 50 mL falcon tube and incubate for 2 h.
Centrifuge cells at 3000 × g for 5 min.
Discard supernatant and resuspend with 100 μL of sterile ddH2O.
Transfer the desired fraction of transformed cells on selective agar plates.
Spread cells using a spreader.
Incubate the agar plates with transformed cells at 30°C for 2–3 days.
Pick 4–10 single yeast colonies and spread the cells on a selective agar plate.
Incubate the spread cells for approximately 20 hours at 30°C.
Validate successful transformants with PCR.
Prepare a Master Mix in an 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube according to manufacturer’s guidelines.
Split the prepared Master Mix into aliquots of 19.5 μL in PCR tubes.
Keep all PCR reagents and mixtures on ice prior to initiating the PCR reaction.
Inoculate a small amount of yeast colonies into Eppendorf tubes containing 50 μL NaOH 20 mM.
Vortex the tubes with yeast cells.
Heat the tubes at 100°C for 5 minutes to lyse the yeast cells.
Centrifuge the tubes at 20000 × g for 1 minute.
Transfer and mix 0.5 μL of each supernatant into PCR reaction tubes.
Place the tubes inside a thermocycler.
Initiate the PCR reaction protocol according to manufacturer’s guidelines.
Measure the O.D.600 of yeast cultures grown overnight in SC medium.
Dilute cells to an O.D.600 of 0.1–0.15 in 2 mL prewarmed SC medium.
Grow the diluted cultures for 2–3 hours at 30°C in a shaker to reach an O.D.600 of 0.3–0.5.
Transfer 300–500 μL of yeast cultures into separate wells of uncoated 8-well Ibidi slides.
Image yeast cultures with a wide-field or confocal fluorescence microscope.
Use the appropriate light source and beam splitter-filter set for examining the expression level of 2E2-FP.
Image WT strain simultaneously for comparison, especially when 2E2-FP is expressed from the weak URA3 promoter.
If using a 2E2-FP version with NLS, only image the cell nucleus.
Inoculate one or two colonies in 5 mL prewarmed YPD medium supplemented with appropriate antibiotic reagent(s).
Grow yeast cultures at 30°C in a shaker.
Mix yeast cultures with 50% glycerol in a 1:1 ratio in Eppendorf or Cryovial tubes.
Store glycerol stocks at −80°C.
Amplify the HA cassette using high-fidelity polymerase.
Prepare a Master Mix containing four to eight 25 μL PCR reactions in an Eppendorf tube.
Pipette 25 μL into PCR tubes or strip tubes for a total of 100-200 μL PCR product.
Initiate the PCR reaction with a two-step cycling protocol.
Verify the successful amplification of the HA cassette.
Mix extension primers to further amplify the PCR product, enhancing homology with the gene of interest (optional).
Store PCR products at −20°C for future use.
Transform 3HA or 6HA cassettes into yeast strains expressing 2E2-FP using 100–200 μL of PCR product from step 4.
Select and validate successfully HA-transformed yeast colonies.
Store transformants and colony plates at 4°C, wrapped with parafilm for up to 1–2 weeks (optional).
Long-term store yeast strains as glycerol stocks at −80°C.
Inoculate stored yeast strains into prewarmed medium for imaging.
Perform live cell fluorescent imaging of HA-tagged protein of interest labeled with 2E2-FP.
Inoculate the yeast strains from an agar plate or glycerol stock into 5 mL prewarmed SC medium in a 50 mL falcon tube.
Grow the inoculated cultures at 30°C in a shaker.
Measure the O.D.600 of the yeast cultures the next day.
Dilute cells to O.D.600 = 0.1–0.15 in 2 mL prewarmed SC medium in 50 mL falcon tubes.
Grow diluted cells for 2–3 h in a shaker at 30°C to an O.D.600 of 0.3–0.5.
Briefly vortex the cell cultures.
Transfer 300–500 μL of yeast cultures into separate wells of ConA-coated 8-well Ibidi slides for immobilization.
Incubate the yeast cultures at 25°C for 10–15 min according to desired confluence on the slide.
Remove the medium from the wells.
Gently pipette fresh 500 μL prewarmed SC medium into the wells and discard it.
Repeat washing steps 1–2 times if necessary.
Add 350 μL prewarmed SC medium into the wells for final immobilization.
Image the immobilized yeast cells with a wide-field or confocal microscope inside a temperature-controlled enclosure.
Set the fluorescent microscope temperature to 30°C at least 2–3 h prior to microscopy experiment.
Choose the objective lens according to the magnification preference.
Use 1 × 1 binning in the camera settings, if applicable.
Select the appropriate light source - beam splitter - filter set for excitation and detection of the fluorescent protein.
Excite the fluorescent protein using the selected wavelength (e.g., 390 nm, 488 nm, 590 nm, or 640 nm).
Use bright-field or DIC to visualize yeast cell morphology.
Adjust illumination intensity and exposure time according to the fluorescent intensity of the labeled protein.
Acquire multiple Z-slices for detection throughout the whole cell body (e.g., 12 Z-slices with 800 nm steps).
Excite cells periodically in preferred intervals for time-lapse experiments.
Save microscopy experiment output as photos or video files.
Proceed with image analysis.
